title: A resumed session whose worktree is gone makes a fresh worktree before it writes, not work on main
why: shiv, Oct 29 16:49 CDT: on his computer, a session that lost its worktree and was resumed just worked in the main checkout instead of first making a new worktree. Today only agents are covered: decision an-agent-outside-its-home-tree-must-stop (guard rule worktree-home) makes an agent stop when its home is gone, from its record in <git-common-dir>/agent-homes/. A top-level session has no home record, so after a resume in the primary checkout nothing stops it writing there.
note: Scope (triage 12): record a top-level session's worktree the way worktree-home records an agent's (by session id, in the git common dir). On resume, session_start.sh sees the record, the folder gone and the cwd in the primary, and prints one line: make a worktree (EnterWorktree, from the recorded branch if it still exists, else from origin) before any write. The guard refuses a write into the primary from such a session until it does. Red first: a resumed session with a removed worktree writes into the primary today. Cost: one file per session, written once; read inside the hooks already running. Risk: incident (shiv's report, Oct 29). Needs no answer: his report sets the behaviour. Cloud: yes, with a test that removes a worktree. Port: yes, the hooks load in every repo. Placed ahead of the open owner steps (triage 12, Oct 29): built, waits on batch 25.
